blind_flags.note: A is somewhat defensible: the essay explicitly explains where the name 'Zipper' came from (sentences 9-10). D is best only under the usual ACT reading that 'primary purpose' means the essay as a whole, and most of this essay covers the fastener's technical development. Also, A's 'named a line of boots after the sound they made' is a slight paraphrase: the passage says the president enjoyed the sound and so named the boots. Consider adding a stronger cue to the stem (e.g., 'primarily to explain') or making the naming paragraph clearly subordinate.

results.blind_notes: Paragraphs 1-2 (and much of 3) cover the invention and refinement of the fastener; the naming takes up only sentences 9-10. So D. B: the description of the teeth is about development, not the name. C is factually false, because the passage does explain where the word came from.

blind2_flags.note: A is a strong rival. Paragraph 3 fully explains how 'zipper' came about, and the essay also traces earlier names ('clasp locker', 'hookless fastener'), so a student could argue the naming thread runs throughout. D is better because two of the four paragraphs are about mechanism and development, and naming is one paragraph. Still, the A-vs-D distinction depends on the 'primary purpose' convention. It would be worth making the development material even more dominant, or tightening A so it is clearly too narrow.
